score.note: First pass. Family-matcher assigned games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c (080ce85c, score 8031/10000) as template, but the owner's own 904 retained bytes (games/gs1/asm/080cc5d8.s) show a genuinely different shape: this owner allocates its own kind-39/40/41 heap blocks via Func_080048b0(kind,size) instead of reading pre-existing ones from *(void**)0x03001EEC, iterates a fixed 56-frame loop (not member_count*16+48), drives a single Func_080e396c(object->field8, screen) projection per frame instead of looping the party, and layers in a 128-entry fixed-address 0x02010000 'star' seed, a second 64-entry star-record array inside its own work block at +0x7080, and a transient kind-47 four-sprite decoration burst. The original scalar callback model accidentally let GCC overlap rectangle1 with other locals, producing a 36-byte frame even though the reference proves a 40-byte frame with trail_source@sp+8, rectangle[0]@sp+12, rectangle[1]@sp+16, canvas@sp+20, object@sp+24 and screen@sp+28. Reconstructing the callbacks as the family-standard `rectangle[2]` array and swapping canvas/trail_source declaration order recovers every one of those offsets. Naming the 0x03001388 WordCopyFn and the 0x480 scheduler interval reproduces the reference argument-materialization order and extends the byte-exact prefix from 7 to 183 instructions. Finally, one shared `display_base = (void *)0x04000028` local models the reference's reuse of the BG2X base across the conditional BLDALPHA write; the old pair of independent constant casts made GCC rematerialize 0x04000052 and added four downstream bytes. Fresh score is candidate=904/reference=904, differing_halfwords=70, wrong_instructions=56, topology equal. This is a reduction from the pre-reconstruction 223/96 floor with exact extent restored. Remaining work starts at the per-frame projection call's screen-base carrier and the r0/r2/r3 frame-value schedule. Pointer-before-call, pointer-after-call, named screen_x, whole-loop screen-pointer, volatile-screen, and mutating-display-pointer spellings are neutral or regress and were rejected.

rejected_experiments: Inlining the kind-47 decoration draw's x/y expressions directly into the DrawRectangleFn call's argument list instead of pre-computing them into named `x`/`y` locals: compiles but regresses wrong_instructions 96 -> 104 (the reference's instruction order reads the two signed-byte tables before the Data_03001e50[47] callback read, which only happens when x/y are separate statements ahead of the assignment).

Hoisting `(u8*)work + offset` into its own named `u8 *sprite_base` pointer local declared before the kind-47 loop, matching the intuition that a persistent pointer should get its own stack slot: produced byte-identical output to the plain inline `(u8*)work+offset` expression at the call site -- this compiler already performs the hoist on its own regardless of how the source names it, confirming the hoist-vs-recompute choice is register-pressure-driven inside the compiler, not something the surface C syntax controls.

Pre-computing `DrawRectangleFn *rect47_slot = (DrawRectangleFn*)&Data_03001e50[47];` before the loop and dereferencing `*rect47_slot` each iteration, hoping to force the same stack-slot spill the reference shows for kind 47's callback: produced byte-identical output to plain `Data_03001e50[47]` re-evaluated each iteration (both fold to the same link-time-constant address either way); did not by itself create or remove the sp+16 spill seen in the reference.

Cross-edition relocation-aware verification on 2026-08-31 locates this owner in all six releases and proves all 632 non-relocation core bytes identical. The owner has 36 Thumb call relocations and 32 literal fields; every remaining regional byte difference is confined to those fields.

A shipped compiler-route and pass sweep on 2026-08-31 tested routed GCC 2.96, explicit GCC 2.96, old-agbcc, regmove, both schedulers, CSE follow/skip blocks, GCSE, expensive optimizations, thread jumps, strength reduction, rerun-CSE-after-loop, function CSE, and deferred pops. The annotation-free permuter's finite allocator decoder named one low-register expression constraint but refused to search because no unique source repair follows from it. This is the required negative verdict, not an invitation to force allocation. Combined with the already-recorded pointer placement, screen-coordinate, display-base, callback-array, and stack-layout source probes, the ordinary-C axis is closed.

Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect that allocates a work block, a 16KB canvas, and a small trail-sprite buffer; sets BG2 affine scale and blend alpha; loads a palette selected by a 4-way switch on the target object's kind field; seeds a fixed-address 128-entry particle array (side effect, unused by this function) and a 64-entry in-work 'star' record array; registers a 48x48 rectangle-blit callback (kind 46); then runs 56 frames. Each frame re-projects a single tracked point to screen space, shakes BG2's horizontal offset and (after frame 49) fades BLDALPHA, cues a sound/vibration effect once at frame 26, draws a large kind-46 sprite during frames 28-48, bursts four small kind-47 decorations during frames 0-14 from ROM-table-driven offsets, and advances/draws up to 64 sparkle-trail squares whose radius and screen position come from a sine/cosine sweep of each record's stored angle.

Field offsets 0x77b4/0x77b8 on the work block are new to this owner (no precedent in the sibling dossiers); left as raw M2C_FIELD offsets rather than guessing names, matching this family's established practice for byte-offset accesses with no evidence-backed structure yet.
